column2: O drop, you are the winner of cattle, of men, of horses and of strength; the ancient soul of the sacrifice.
For us, O drop, flow the strength of honey with the stream, like Parjanya the rain-giver.
Win and conquer, flowing Soma, great fame; then make us richer.
Win light, win heaven, and all good fortune, Soma; then make us richer.
Win skill and wisdom; drive away the enemies, Soma; then make us richer.
O purifiers, cleanse the soma for Indra to drink; then make us richer.
Grant us a share of the Sun by your skill and your helps; then make us richer.
By your skill and your helps may we long see the Sun; then make us richer.
Flow, well-armed Soma, wealth for both grasses; then make us richer.
Flow unfailing, racer, the overcomer in battles; then make us richer.
They strengthened you with sacrifices, flowing one, in the rite; then make us richer.
Bring us, O drop, wondrous wealth with horses, a full life; then make us richer.
The ruddy one knows the treasures of the mortal, the divine help; the joyful one crosses over, he runs.
From the two of many men, we give thousands; the joyful one crosses over, he runs.
From those two, thirty by the stretch, and thousands, we give; the joyful one crosses over, he runs.
These somas have been released, praised, for great strength, with the stream of the most exhilarating.
Purifying, you go toward the cattle-gifts, the manly wealth, for the feast; flow around, winner of strength.
And all our cattle-rich nourishments, praised on every side, flow, praised by Jamadagni.
We bring fuel and make offerings to you, we, noting every joint; for life, Agni, bring the thoughts to completion; in your friendship may we not come to harm.
May we be able to kindle you; bring our thoughts to completion; in you the gods eat the poured offering; bring the Adityas, for we long for them, Agni; in your friendship may we not come to harm.
At the rising of the sun I praise Mitra and Varuna, Aryaman, devourer of foes.
With golden wealth, this thought is for unharmed strength; this is for the sage's gaining of wisdom.
May we be yours, god Varuna, yours, Mitra, with the patrons; may we receive strength and light.
Whatever of the all-pervading one, given by you, is known — bring that desirable wealth.
You are the priests of the sacrifice, the winners of strength in rites; Indra and Agni, know it.
Swift, chariot-driving, Vritra-slayers, unconquered, Indra and Agni, know it.
Men have milked this exhilarating honey of yours by stones; Indra and Agni, know it.
The sages, knowers of words, adorn you, the sustainer; the Ayus cleanse you.
May Mitra, Aryaman and Varuna drink your essence, O seer, and the Maruts that of the flowing.
Cleansed with good hands, you drive the speech into the sea; you flow, purifying, toward tawny, abundant, much-desired wealth.
Purified in the sheep's wool, flowing, the bull roared in the wood; for the gods, Soma, flowing, you go anointed with cows, to the appointed place.
This one the ten fingers cleanse, the child of the river, together with the Adityas he has been seen.
With Indra and Vayu the pressed one goes to the filter, together with the rays of the sun.
For us, flow honeyed for Bhaga, Vayu and Pushan; lovely for Mitra and Varuna.
Indeed, one like you, yoked of himself, boldly toward the singers, would drive the axle between two wheels.
When, O hundred-powered, you fulfill the wish of the singers, you drive the axle with your powers.
Come to our pressings; O soma-drinker, drink the soma; the exhilaration is a cow-giver for the wealthy.
Then may we know your nearest favors; do not look beyond us; come.
Like a long goad you bear power, O thoughtful one; as with the earlier foot, bounteous, you restrain like Yama the one who goes astray. The divine mother bore you; the auspicious mother bore you.
Loosen the firm hold of the mortal who plots harm; make that one go under who would enslave us. The divine mother bore you; the auspicious mother bore you.
You are the sage, you the seer; the honey of the drink is born; in joys you are the all-sustainer.
In you all the gods, together-minded, obtained drinking; in joys you are all-sustaining.
Whose soma Indra drinks, whose the Maruts, whose Aryaman and Bhaga — with whom we bring Mitra and Varuna and the great Indra for help.
Like a calf with its mothers, the drop, being urged, is anointed; the god-protecting exhilaration, adorned by thoughts.
This one is for the accomplishing of skill; this for strength and feast; this, pressed, is most honeyed for the gods.
The somas flow, the drops, best finders of a way for us; friendly, sounding, blameless, thoughtful, finders of heaven.
Those purified, wise somas, mixed with curds, shining like suns, moving, firm in the ghee.
Pressing with stones, gathered on the cow's skin, they have sounded around for us the nourishment, the finders of wealth.
Flow with this, flow with these riches, run into the lake, O drop of Indra; whose swiftness, like the wind, even the much-wise sets in the man.
And flow for us in this manner, to the ford of the famed, the praiseworthy; sixty thousand riches of Naiguta, shaking like a ripe tree for battle.
Great is this name of his, O bull, for the strong; in the lake or in the slaying place; the Naiguta lulled the unconscious ones, softened them, and drove off the foes.
Agni is the Vasu, famed for wealth; approach most splendid and give wealth.
You, O most brilliant, shining one, we now ask for favor for our friends.
May Indra, with the Adityas, bring to completion for us the sacrifice, our body, and offspring.
May Indra with the Adityas and the Maruts, with his troop, make remedies for us.
The Maruts, of fair hymns, sing the hymn; the famed youth, Indra, makes the response.
The swans, thirsty, have gone to the lovely home in troops of bulls; the friends proclaim together the unyielding, noisy flowing soma.
He yokes the speed of the wide-singing, playing in vain; the cows do not measure him; sharp-horned he makes his circuit; by day he is seen as bay, by night as straight.
The sounding somas like chariots, like horses desiring help, have gone forth for wealth.
Like urged chariots, they have been held in the hands, like the loads of workers.
Like kings with praises, the somas are anointed with cows, like a sacrifice with its seven supporters.
Drinking, they urge the Dawns' fortune of Vivasvat; the suns spread the fine thread.
The ancient singers open the doors of the thoughts, the Ayus for the bull's wrath.
The priests, born of seven, have come together, filling the place of the one.
From navel to navel I take for us, O Sun, for sight with the eye; I milk the offspring of the seer.
The Sun sees with his eye the dear seat of heaven, set in the hidden, by the Adhvaryus.
The drops, of fair glory, have been released along the path of the law of truth, knowing its stages.
The foremost stream of honey plunges into the great waters, to be praised in every offering.
Foremost of speech, with his yoke, the bull roared in the wood, true toward the dwelling, the rite.
When the seer, purifying, flows around with poetry and manly power, the heaven-finder seeks to win.
Flowing toward rivals, he sits among the clans like a king, when the creators praise him.
The dear bay one sits in the sheep's wool, in the woods; the roaring one conquers by thought.
He goes with exhilaration together with Vayu, Indra and the Ashvins, who rejoices by his law.
To Mitra, Varuna, Bhaga the waves of honey flow, knowing it by his powers.
For us, heaven and earth, for the winning of wealth, honey and strength — fame and treasures won together.
Come to the joyful, to the choice one; to the sage, to the thoughtful; to the protector, to the much-desired.
Come to wealth, to the good-minded, to the skilful one in bodies; to the protector, to the much-desired.
The head of heaven, the lord of earth, Vaishvanara, Agni born in the order of truth; the seer, sovereign, guest of men — the gods who sat near made him their cup.
All the gods sing to you, immortal, at your birth, like a child; by your skills they attained immortality, O Vaishvanara, when you shone for your parents.
They sing to the navel of the sacrifices, the seat of wealth, the great invoked; the gods begot Vaishvanara, the charioteer of the rites, the banner of the sacrifice.
Sing for your Mitra and Varuna with a wise song the great, truth-bearing power.
The two sovereigns, ghee-sourced, Mitra and Varuna, gods praised among the gods.
Make us able for the great earthly and heavenly wealth; great is your power among the gods.
Come, Indra of wondrous splendor; these somas, pressed, yearn for you, purified by the fingers.
Come, Indra, urged by thought, impelled by sages, to the one who has pressed; to the prayers of the priests.
Come, Indra, hastening, to the prayers, O lord of bay horses; at the pressing accept our offering.
Praise him who with his flame embraces all woods and makes black with his tongue.
The mortal who, kindled, serves Indra's favor wins splendor, crossing the waters.
Fill for us strength-rich nourishments, swift ones, and horses, to carry Indra and Agni.
The drop has gone forth to the appointed place of Indra; the friend does not break the friend's promise; Soma flows into the vessel like a man to women, by the hundred-course path.
Your thoughts, delighting, praising, honoring, have advanced to the shelters; they sang to the bay one at play; the cows have gathered toward him with milk.
Soma, bring us regulated, swelling nourishment, O drop; flow purified with a wave, which milks for us thrice daily, unfailing, rich in strength, honey, and heroic vigor.
No work perishes of him who has made the ever-growing one; by sacrifices praise Indra, all-praised, skilful, unassailable, bold in strength.
The unconquerable, fierce, victorious in battles, in whom the great ones, the widely moving, as he is born the cows lowed and the heavens and earths lowed.
Release together like a calf with its mothers the house-prosperer, the god-guarding exhilaration, of double strength.
Cleanse the skill-accomplisher, as for strength and feast, as most blessed for Mitra and Varuna.
The racer with axle, thousand-streamed, has gone forth across the filter, through the woolen sieve.
That axle-racer, of a thousand seeds, is cleansed by waters, mingled with cows.
Go forth, Soma, to Indra's belly, held by men, pressed by stones.
The somas pressed far away, and those pressed near, and those in Sharyanavat.
